metadata.source: research/branches/chicago_burlington_and_quincy_railroad.txt; Feb 1952 Official Guide of the Railways (Burlington Lines section), full OCR cached at research/sources/official_guide_1952.txt; branchline.uk (John Fowler), Passenger Stations & Stops, illinoisrrs2 / iowarrs / nebraskarrs / missourirrs
metadata.geometry_method: Overpass corridor fetch per branch (all railway ways: rail, abandoned, disused, razed, dismantled), Dijkstra over a graph in which ways tagged old_railway_operator=CB&Q cost 1x and everything else 3x, waypoints taken from the research report's own via lists and snapped by a dynamic program over up to eight candidate nodes each, with each leg confined to a corridor around its own straight line so the router cannot wander onto a parallel railroad. Every feature's geometry_quality gives its traced length against the report's documented mileage and names any straight-line legs.
metadata.not_yet_sourced: EVERY BRANCH IN THIS FILE THAT ENDS IN 1952 HAS AN UNKNOWN, WITHHELD END YEAR. The Feb 1952 Official Guide is a single snapshot: it proves the trains were running in September 1951 and says nothing about when they stopped. The Burlington's branch passenger service was swept away somewhere between about 1952 and 1968 and NOT ONE of those discontinuances has been dated by any source consulted. A 1952 end here is where the evidence stops, not where the trains stopped -- do not 'fix' one by rounding it up. Nor is a start year the year a line opened: it is the earliest year a timetable proves, usually a branchline.uk Official-Guide snapshot letter (1875, 1884 or 1893), and the lines are older than the map shows. branchline.uk cannot close a Burlington branch, only open one: outside Nebraska's single d = 1950t there is NO lettered timetable snapshot for the CB&Q between 1893 and 1976 in any of Fowler's state files, and the Missouri CB&Q legend is blank in every position. Still unexploited, and the highest-value source left for this railroad: the 1952 Guide's index of stations carries a per-station freight-only dagger across the whole 11,000-mile system, but the OCR has mangled that dagger into at least four different characters and it was not used.

properties.line: Chicago, Burlington and Quincy: Edgemont – Deadwood
properties.speed_source: estimated, NOT sourced: a secondary branch of this era, taken from the kind of service the Feb 1952 Guide shows (Table 23) rather than from any timetable's running times
properties.geometry_quality: Real trace from OpenStreetMap: a Dijkstra shortest path over every railway way (rail, abandoned, disused, razed, dismantled) in a corridor around the route, with ways tagged old_railway_operator=CB&Q costed at 1x and all other track at 3x, so the path stays on the Burlington's own alignment wherever OSM records it. Snapped to the report's own station list; every one of the 10 waypoints lies within 1.8 km of the drawn line. OSM lines followed: George S. Mickelson Trail 73 mi; [abandoned] 17 mi; [rail] 2 mi; Burlington Road 0 mi. TRACED LENGTH 109.5 mi against a DOCUMENTED 107 mi (+2%). APPROXIMATED: 23.1 mi of the total is straight-line, drawn across 2 place(s) where the grade is lifted and OSM has no way at all -- Hot Springs-Pringle 12.6 mi; Hill City-Mystic 10.6 mi. Those legs are ruled lines, not survey. ERA NOTE: much of the surviving alignment is today's BNSF, which is the CB&Q's own successor on this route, so the modern centreline is the historical one; where the line is abandoned the trace follows the recorded grade. Simplified to a 20 m Douglas-Peucker tolerance.

segments.note: the Burlington's Black Hills lines were standard-gauged and completed to Deadwood in 1890-1891; the bracket is collapsed inward to 1891. Feb 1952 Table 23 heads its columns "Mix." and shows times -- a mixed train still carrying passengers. THE 1952 END IS THE LAST CONFIRMED YEAR, NOT A KNOWN END. No source consulted dates when passenger service actually stopped here; the Burlington's branch trains were swept away somewhere between about 1952 and 1968 and not one of those discontinuances has been dated. The end year is a withheld unknown, not an abandonment -- DO NOT extend this line to a rounder year without evidence. Equally, 1891 is the earliest year positively CONFIRMED, not the year the line opened: the branch is older than the map shows, and the confirmed start is deliberately late rather than guessed early. The scenic Black Hills line through Custer and Rochford. This mixed train was one of the last of its kind on the system. Headway is an estimate and is NOT sourced.
